spec_match.rationale: The four target keywords, the name lookup, and the new-context fallback are taken from the rules for choosing a navigable and linked to it. The pages never assert what the removal will do from a build that predates it: the before behaviour is measured, and the after behaviour is inferred from a separate measurement of an underscore-prefixed name that no engine special-cases.

interactive.rationale: Three live experiments in a real frame tree — a single click, a seven-row sweep, and a name-resolution proof — plus a paste-in auditor that reclassifies on every press. Every navigation is a real click on a real link; nothing is simulated or narrated.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Each card promises one observable outcome and the page delivers exactly that outcome as a table row or a verdict line.

edge_cases.rationale: The uppercase spelling _CURRENT is swept because keyword matching is ASCII case-insensitive, and it reaches the same branch. The auditor separates keyword, matched name, reserved underscore shape, and new-context cases, and _top and _blank are resolved but not fired, with the reason stated rather than the row omitted.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus, both relevant HTML specification sections, and the usage metric the removal cites.

conformance.rationale: Four assertions, all side-effect free or self-cleaning: verbatim target reflection including case, verbatim frame-name reflection with a leading underscore, the attribute existing on all four targetable interfaces, and named lookup finding a frame. 4 pass / 0 fail on all four pages.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Driven on Chrome 150.0.7871.128 over CDP. Recorded: target="_current" navigated the source frame and left the sibling named _current untouched; target="_CURRENT" did the same; target="sidecar" navigated the sidecar frame; target="_self" navigated the source frame; target="_parent" navigated the harness; and target="_notakeyword" navigated the frame named _notakeyword.

telemetry_health.rationale: Console output is one namespaced line per action; no errors or unhandled rejections in any of the four pages.

design_system.rationale: Shared stylesheet and tokens throughout, house stage/table/verdict patterns, inline SVG rather than emoji in the one iconed verdict.

accessibility.rationale: Every control is a button with a visible label and a 44px minimum target, every iframe has a title, verdicts are role=status with aria-live so a change is announced, tables have captions and scoped headers, and focus-visible outlines are explicit.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Frame grids collapse to a single column under min-width tracks, tables scroll inside their own containers, and the harness iframe is width-constrained rather than fixed.

openQuestions.title: The after behaviour is inferred, not measured
openQuestions.detail: No Chrome 153 or later was available to build against, so the pages record the pre-removal outcome and infer the post-removal one from a name that behaves the way _current will. The inference is sound and stated on the page, but the day a 153+ build is to hand, every page should be re-driven and the recorded outcome checked against the prediction.

openQuestions.title: window.open is described but not exercised
openQuestions.detail: The rewrite section says the same lookup applies to window.open(url, "_current") and to form targets, and neither is driven — a popup is not something a demo should open unasked, and a form target would need a server route. The claim rests on the shared definition rather than on a measurement here.

guidanceConsulted: modern-web-guidance: interactive over static, evidence over assertion
AGENTS.md: for removals and deprecations, pair detection with a working replacement pattern
summary: A removal demonstrated as a difference you can watch: a frame tree containing a frame genuinely named _current, a real click, and a report of which frame moved. The pages read the tree rather than the user agent, so they give the correct answer on both sides of the removal, and the one claim that cannot be measured on a pre-removal build is tested by proxy and labelled as such.
